incidents.name: SpankChain LedgerChannel reentrancy
incidents.notes: LedgerChannel opened a channel with an attacker-controlled ERC20 whose transfer() re-entered LCOpenTimeout()/consensusCloseChannel before the channel state was cleared, letting the attacker withdraw the channel's ETH repeatedly.

sources.ref: onchain review: LedgerChannel 0xf91546835f756DA0c10cFa0CDA95b15577b84aA7 created 2018-08-30T09:35:59Z by 0x406fffca2a6d1997b9ef573d67efe74ba786dff1, unrelated to the attack sender; no proxy, no upgrade events, age measured from deployment. USD figure taken from SpankChain's own post-mortem (165.38 ETH, ~$38,000). Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation block 6239908 and the incident block 6467248; the six DELEGATECALLs in the runtime are calls into the ECTools library linked at deploy time (Etherscan's library map records ECTools:0xcb107c7d2a93e638b20342f46b10b9b6d81377bf, present as a PUSH20 constant in the bytecode), an address that cannot be repointed, and none of them is taken in the exploit trace.
